scope: Primary-source examples of linear current amplifiers for a clean force-control prototype. Illustrative capability, not a part list or hardware qualification.

preferredRepresentative.datasheetDate: December2014; linked by current manufacturer product page on2026-09-30
preferredRepresentative.driveType: Linear brushed/voice-coil current (torque) or voltage (velocity) amplifier
preferredRepresentative.bandwidthDefinitionLimit: Datasheet does not label the5kHz value as a specific3dB/phase criterion and does not specify the test resistance, bus, amplitude or bias. It does not establish response on our3mH/4ohm coil at24V.
preferredRepresentative.outputVoltageStatement: Up to +/-43V equivalent motor voltage, dependent on motor load. Actual24V delivered output/headroom is not tabulated.

SOA_visualInspection.xAxis: Drive voltage = supply voltage - winding voltage

preferredRepresentative.inference: The24V static50N/20N-per-A,4ohm point is2.5A and35W driver heat, within the shown50W and100W curves. The published5kHz value into2.5mH makes a measured1-2kHz current loop plausible; no achieved prototype bandwidth or noise is claimed.
preferredRepresentative.unpublishedLimit: No quantitative output-current ripple/noise specification was found in the linked datasheet.

alternativeRepresentative.driveType: Single-supply H-bridge linear amplifier with bipolar current command
alternativeRepresentative.datasheetBandwidthCriterion: Nominal current-loop bandwidth, varies with motor inductance
alternativeRepresentative.documentCaution: Current product page and2021 PDF use different voltage and bandwidth descriptions; use current product24-70V range. Datasheet page2 also contains SMA5005 names apparently retained from another source; LCAM5/15 table onpage1 and manualp6 independently identify250W. Neither establishes bandwidth or current-noise performance with our exact coil.
alternativeRepresentative.unpublishedLimit: No quantitative output-current ripple/noise specification was found in the primary sources reviewed.

derivedStaticThermalExamples.assumptions: 50N horizontal normal hold, Kf20N/A,2.5A constant, zero back EMF, ideal linear H-bridge loss approximation. Electronics/fan power excluded. These are analytical calculations, not a thermal simulation.

prototypeRequirements.drive: Bipolar current command and output; >=3.5A capability;24V bus; measured low current ripple; stable tuned current loop with real4ohm/3mH cold/hot winding.
prototypeRequirements.bandwidthQualification: Measure step/Bode response around2.5A bias with small perturbations; identify amplitude-dependent slew/voltage clipping, current noise, command delay, jitter and gain. Fit actual response, do not substitute drive update/carrier frequency for closed-loop bandwidth.
prototypeRequirements.noiseBudgetIllustration: For Kf20N/A and rigid high-frequency force transfer, a0.15N peak residual force budget corresponds to7.5mA peak current error; a0.10N budget corresponds to5mA. Actual allowable ripple depends on measured mechanics and chosen controller margin.
prototypeRequirements.scopeLimit: Native voltage comparisons use averaged voltage and omit PWM ripple, finite force-cell structural resonance and amplifier current-noise spectra. A linear amp reduces switching ripple but its numerical noise performance remains unqualified.
